answer: An account may hold at most five trusted devices, and adding a sixth requires a signed eviction of the oldest one, recorded publicly. A Sybil operator cannot accumulate an army of devices under one account, and each eviction leaves an auditable record, so device farming becomes visible and self-limiting. The design treats each recovery as a nectar: small alone, decisive in aggregate. After the island closes and the ember opens, the recovery is frozen and published for audit.
